# Consider your limitations. When you are ready for a new kitchen or your first kitchen, it is important that you look at what you want to use the kitchen space for as part of your overall living space.

# Ask yourself what you want to do in the kitchen. Do you need a seating area? Will the kitchen double as an office? Does it need to be kid friendly? Will you entertain guests in the kitchen? Do you do a lot of cooking/baking? How much time will you be spending in the kitchen?  All these things and more will need to be considered when planning the layout of the kitchen.
# Lay out your ideas in a virtual room planner. Ikea, Armstrong, Merillat, Kraftmade, and many other companies have online programs in which you can play around with different kitchen styles.

added: [[Category:Home Improvements and Repairs]]

Designing your own kitchen ensures that the lay out and look of the kitchen suits you and your budget not that of the showroom salesman/designer. Simple tips to help you avoid the pit falls when are ready for that new dream kitchen.
== Steps ==
#  When you are ready for a new kitchen or your first kitchen, it is important that you look at what you want to use the kitchen space for as part of your overalle living space.

#   Ask yourself what you want to do in the kitchen, Do you need a seating area, will you need an area to do paper work, do you need somwhere for the children to sit while you work?, will you entertain guests in the kitchen?, do you do a lot of cooking/baking?, do you only prepare simple meals or are you more serious as a cook?,Is the kitchen part of a larger living space?, do you love your kitchen? or is it just somwhere you tolerate because you have to?.
#  All these things and more will need to be considered when planning the lay out of the kitchen.
#  Do you want more information and practical tip? My next posting will do that.
== Tips ==
*Draw a plan of the kitchen area and make sure you mark where the doors and windows are and how high they are.
*Mark where the stop tap and any consumer meters are (this avoids putting an applaince or unit with an appliance in front of where you will what to access these.
*Mark where the light switches are to avoid covering these if you are not prepared or able to alter the electrics.
*Check out where the gas supply is. If you plan to fit gas applainces and have a solid floor this could be difficult to move.
*Also mark any thing else that you believe is important and may effect you design layout.
*When you have all this make sure you re check all the measurements again, it will save you a lot of time and money later.
*Next stage in next posting
== Warnings ==
*Do not attempt to alter any electrical wiring or gas connections unless you are qualified to do so. These are jobs for professionals and in some cases you could break local planning regs.
